item.text: The Royal Commission into Trade Union Governance and Corruption devoted this volume to proposals for law reform.
item.support:
This Volume of the Report is devoted to recommendations in relation 
to law reform.

item.text: It considered union regulation, officials’ duties, corrupting benefits, enterprise bargaining, competition, construction, entry rights and Royal Commission powers.

item.text: The Commission considered that the benefits of national regulation justified governments exploring a single regime for employee and employer organisations.
item.support:
it is considered that the potential 
benefits justify the States and Commonwealth giving consideration to 
implementing a national regime

item.text: It recommended a separate, independent regulator for registered organisations and funding sufficient for that regulator to carry out its functions.
item.support:
The Registered Organisations Commission should 
be an independent stand-alone regulator.

item.quote:
The Registered Organisations Commission should 
be an independent stand-alone regulator.

The Commonwealth government ensure that the registered organisations 
regulator is properly resourced to carry out its functions, with a separate budget 
for which it is accountable.
